questions.subtopic: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
questions.context: In Q. No. 19 and 20 a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option.
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** If the graph of a polynomial touches x-axis at only one point, then the polynomial cannot be a quadratic polynomial.

**Reason (R) :** A polynomial of degree \(n(n > 1)\) can have at most n zeroes.

options.label: A
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not correct explanation for Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subtopic: Median of Grouped Data
questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a photograph of BINGO balls over a number card (printed mostly black in this scan); every number is in the passage and table. Page idx 12.
questions.context:
BINGO is game of chance. The host has 75 balls numbered 1 through 75. Each player has a BINGO card with some numbers written on it. The participant cancels the number on the card when called out a number written on the ball selected at random. Whosoever cancels all the numbers on his/her card, says BINGO and wins the game.

The table given below, shows the data of one such game where 48 balls were used before Tara said 'BINGO'.

| Numbers announced | Number of times |
|---|---|
| 0-15 | 8 |
| 15-30 | 9 |
| 30-45 | 10 |
| 45-60 | 12 |
| 60-75 | 9 |

Based on the above information, answer the following :
questions.stem: Write the median class.
